resources.string: A few taps before yer maiden voyage.
What\'s left to fit out. Nothing you\'ve fitted out changes.
myCar is unofficial: fit it out while parked, then keep your eyes on the road.

Cars only parley with phones holding a certificate they trust. myCar doesn\'t include one: it downloads public ones from open-source projects on GitHub (about 10 KB each). If your car turns one down, myCar tries the next.
A downloaded file wasn\'t the expected certificate, so myCar threw it overboard. Try again later.
Couldn\'t haul in the certificates. Check your internet connection, then try again.
Hauled in %1$d of %2$d. %3$s is ready; you can get the others later in Rigging.
Ready to sail: your own certificate.
Turn myCar on for the ship
It\'s switched off in Rigging, so the ship can\'t hail it.
You\'ll pick myCar for the voyage when you plug in.
Android Auto is on, and it can seize the ship\'s connection before myCar does. On the screen this opens, tap Disable, then OK, then sail back here.

Then keep it. When you plug in, Android asks which app to open: choose myCar and tap Always, and myCar takes the helm. If Android Auto opens by itself, it was set to always open: on its app info, tap Open by default, then Clear defaults.
Skipped. Tap Allow when you\'re ready to sail.

Your car shows who\'s calling and your recent calls, and can dial your contacts, the chart knows where you are, and music can reach the car without Bluetooth. Android asks a few times: tap Allow each time. myCar only reads, and listens only when you tap the mic.
Everything here can wait for a later tide.

The car shows your messages, reads them aloud and lets you send word back. Turn myCar on in the page this opens. If Android says it\'s a restricted setting: open myCar\'s app info, tap ⋮, then Allow restricted settings, and try again.
The helm shows your next event. myCar only reads your calendar.
Lets myCar show that it\'s connected to the car, with Stop while it sends the phone\'s sound, and tell you when a refit is out.
How shanties reach the ship. Calls go over Bluetooth either way.

resources.string: Nothing is scuttled or reset. You\'ll see only what\'s left, with what\'s shipshape ticked.
Take me back to fitting out
myCar is unofficial. No carmaker made or checked it, and it can fail without warning. Fit it out before you go, then keep your eyes on the road.
myCar uses it to send your shanties to the car and to hear you when you ask for something or reply to a message. What you say stays on the phone.
The car\'s chart and nearby searches need it. Without it, the crow\'s nest shows no chart.
The car shows your messages, reads them aloud and lets you send word back. Turn myCar on in the list this opens.
Android Auto is still installed, and like a rival crew it fights myCar for the ship\'s USB connection. Disable or uninstall it on the screen this opens.
If your phone asks which app to open when you plug into the ship, pick myCar and tap Always.
Pick how shanties reach the ship. Calls go over Bluetooth either way.
Ask for directions, shanties, or a call by voice. Your phone turns speech into text by itself, and nothing you say leaves it. It needs %1$d MB, downloaded once. Use Wi-Fi if you can.
Downloading, %1$d%%. You can sail on; it keeps going.
The download ran aground. Tap Download the parrot to try again.
Run this from a computer with USB debugging on, and Android trusts myCar with your audio for good. Without it, you tap Start once each voyage.
While audio goes to the car, Android hides what notifications say, as if you were sharing your screen. This lets myCar show them during a voyage and hide them again after.
Over Bluetooth when your ship takes the phone\'s shanties that way, otherwise through myCar.
No prompt each voyage, and your chart app\'s voice reaches the ship. Some ships take only calls over it.
Over the cable or Wi-Fi, as Android Auto does. Android asks to share audio once each voyage.
We chart our own course and bow to no crown.

resources.string: Spotify and other services play inside myCar, from their own web player. Sign on once on the phone with your own account, in Rigging > Shanties. Stow the phone\'s Spotify app there: one Spotify aboard, not two.
Close the shanty box beside the chart and a wee shanty box floats over it, with the cover and its buttons: hold it, then drag it anywhere. Beside the chart, the shanty box now goes up to Extra large.
Shanty verses are found far more often, and every haul is checked, so another shanty\'s words never show up. Instrumental tracks say so.
The chart gets your position even with the phone locked in your pocket: myCar takes it as the car arrives. If Android still refuses, the car tells you, only when you\'re stopped.

All the helm\'s rigging is on the phone too, in Rigging > Helm: change any of it and the ship follows at once, even mid-voyage. So are the decks beside the chart and the apps stowed away from the fleet.

Tap the mic, or press the talk button on your wheel, and speak. Your phone turns speech into text by itself, and what you say stays on it, unless you ask your own Home Assistant. Say \"%1$s\" aboard for the full list.

Tap the mic, or press the talk button on your wheel, and speak. Your phone turns speech into text by itself, and what you say stays on it, unless you ask your own Home Assistant. It listens and answers in %1$s, myCar\'s tongue. Say \"%2$s\" aboard for the full list.
The phone\'s shanties pause while its screen is shared

Open myCar on the phone to share its screen at the helm
Another app seized the car\'s connection before myCar could. If Android asks which app to open for the car, choose myCar.
